topic: A dollar a day from birth at seven percent
hook: A dollar a day from birth could grow to almost half a million dollars.
cta: Follow for one money rule a day.

captions.hook_line: $1 a day from birth could grow to about $480,000 by 65 at 7% a year. Here's the math 📈
captions.body: That is $23,725 put in over 65 years; compound growth at an assumed 7% average does the rest. Real returns vary and are never guaranteed.
captions.share_line: Send this to a new parent.

sources.claim: Compound interest with monthly deposits (SEC calculator)

visual_style: Photorealistic cinematic film still, natural daylight, real materials and textures, shallow depth of field

blocks.narration: A dollar a day, starting the day you're born, could grow to almost half a million dollars by the time you turn sixty-five.
blocks.visual: A newborn baby's tiny hand gripping a single crisp one-dollar bill on a soft white blanket

shots.visual: A newborn baby's tiny hand gripping a single crisp one-dollar bill on a soft white blanket
shots.action: The baby's fingers curl tighter around the bill; the camera slowly pushes in

shots.visual: A large glass jar on a wooden table filled with dollar bills and coins
shots.action: Bills and coins pour into the jar from above until it overflows onto the table; the camera pulls back

shots.visual: A cheerful silver-haired woman on a sunny porch holding a birthday cake with lit candles
shots.action: She blows out the candles and laughs as the smoke curls up

blocks.narration: Here's the math. Three hundred sixty-five dollars a year, invested every month, earning seven percent a year on average.
blocks.visual: Overhead view of hundreds of one-dollar bills laid out in neat rows on a dark wooden table

shots.visual: Overhead view of hundreds of one-dollar bills laid out in neat rows on a dark wooden table
shots.action: The camera glides slowly over the rows as the bills ripple in a breeze

shots.visual: A hand placing a small stack of dollar bills into a clear glass piggy bank on a wooden table
shots.action: The hand drops the bills in and the pile inside grows; warm light glows from inside the piggy bank

blocks.narration: In sixty-five years you'd put in about twenty-four thousand dollars. Compound growth adds the other four hundred fifty-eight thousand.
blocks.visual: A modest stack of dollar bills next to a small brass calculator on a wooden table

shots.visual: A modest stack of dollar bills next to a small brass calculator on a wooden table
shots.action: A hand pats the short stack down and slides it to the center of the table

shots.visual: The same wooden table with a stack of dollar bills rising tall into the air
shots.action: The stack grows rapidly upward past the top of the frame as the camera tilts up to follow it

blocks.narration: The trick is time. Most of that growth happens in the last twenty years, when your earnings start earning their own.
blocks.visual: A large antique brass hourglass on a desk, filled with gold coins instead of sand

shots.visual: A large antique brass hourglass on a desk, filled with gold coins instead of sand
shots.action: Gold coins trickle through the hourglass and the pile below grows faster and faster

shots.visual: A row of gold coins on a dark wooden table under warm light
shots.action: Each coin splits into two, then those split again, spreading across the table; the camera pulls back

blocks.narration: Real markets rise and fall, and nothing is guaranteed, but every story like this starts with something this small:
blocks.visual: A roller coaster car on a tall wooden track against a sunset sky

shots.visual: A roller coaster car on a tall wooden track against a sunset sky
shots.action: The car climbs, dips sharply, then climbs higher than before; the camera follows it

shots.visual: A tiny green seedling sprouting from a single gold coin half-buried in a small clay pot of soil on a wooden table, warm light
shots.action: The seedling slowly unfurls its first two leaves as the camera pushes in
